Should europoors hedge?

Open thread • Replies: 53 • Updated: 2026-09-29 21:52 UTC

OP

As a European holding US stock indexes you are constantly affected by the USD to euro exchange rate. Most often this has actually worked in European holders' favour, because the euro weakened, thus inadvertently giving euros better returns on US stocks than to Americans.
Recently the trend has reversed however. 2025 in particular was an absolute bloodbath, of what should've been nearly 20% gains on the S&P euros were left with only 5% because of the weakening of the USD.
You could protect against this by buying a hedged index that uses future contracts to undo the effects of the exchange rate between the currencies, but then that would also leave you with lower returns if the dollar were to strengthen.

What is /biz/'s opinion on the matter? Hedged or unhedged? It's essentially just speculating on if the USD strengthens or weakens against the euro in the long term.

Almost every day, you can see an inverse relationship between USD/EUR and SP500, and as somebody said, the SP500 in EUR is smoother than the regular one.
There is alot of arbitrage between FX, SP500 and bond rates, the market almost looks efficient.

Sometimes, like during the eurozone crisis, the FX rates move a lot for other reasons. Then you can get fucked (or gain a lot) for holding in a foreign currency. Personally, I see more upside in being un-hedge.
